title: Do Neurons Operate in Binary States?
summary: Neurons fire *all‑or‑none* spikes, but their true information processing is **not binary**: it involves analog integration, firing rate, timing, and distributed codes across populations.

content_html:
Do Neurons Operate in Binary States?

Neurons fire all‑or‑none spikes, but their true information processing is not binary: it involves analog integration, firing rate, timing, and distributed codes across populations.

Aspect Neuron Transistor
Unit output Spike (all-or-none) 0/1 voltage level
Inputs Many graded EPSPs/IPSPs Single/few inputs
Information code Rate, timing, population Boolean logic
Noise handling Probabilistic, robust Noise margins
Plasticity Adaptive (learning) Fixed (unless reprogrammed)
